findings.title: Task 2 cannot meet "the full `tests/metrology/` suite passes unchanged"
findings.description:
`LanguageSnapshot._one_measurement_per_metric` (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot_models.py:185-193`) rejects any section missing a `SnapshotMetric` member. Two existing fixtures hand-list exactly the four 400 metrics:

- `python_snapshot()` in `test_render.py:31-65`, used by both render tests.
- `test_json_round_trip_is_lossless` in `tests/metrology/snapshot/test_snapshot_models.py:225-253`.

Once Task 2 adds the four enum members, both raise "missing metrics", so at least three tests fail before the first commit. Task 2 only anticipates the `PythonAdapter.metrics` break.

Fix: add a Task 2 step that extends those two fixtures with absent measurements for the new metrics, and reword the success line to "passes with only those fixture additions".

findings.title: Task 4's Python fixture score of 6 contradicts Task 3's counting rules
findings.description:
Task 3 (line 54, from D2) counts "1 per `for` plus 1 per `if`" in a comprehension. A comprehension `if` always comes with a `for`, so the Success Criterion 3 fixture scores 7, not 6:

- base 1, `if` 1, `elif` 1, `and` 1, comprehension `for` 1, comprehension `if` 1, `except` 1.

The contradiction is inherited from the slice design (D2 at line 139 against Success Criterion 3 at line 266), and the task file copies both sides. An implementer following Task 3 fails Task 4, and must either drop the comprehension `for` from the definition or change the expected value. Either choice silently alters a metric that 403 and 420 consume.

Line 63 has the same slip: "one test per decision point, each scoring 2" cannot hold for a comprehension `if` or an `elif`, which score at least 3.

Fix: decide 6 or 7 in the slice design, then align Tasks 3 and 4. The TypeScript fixture is consistent (1 + `if` + `??` + ternary + 2 cases = 6).

findings.title: Task 7's "edited only for the rename" is not achievable with a required `complexity` field
findings.description:
`FunctionLength` is built positionally with four arguments at `test_lengths.py:104-106` and `test_render.py:36`. Adding `complexity: int` breaks all four call sites. The implementer must either add a fifth argument, which is more than a rename, or give the field a default, which the project's no-magic-defaults rule forbids.

Task 7 also never names `test_render.py`, which imports `FunctionLength` at line 9.

Fix: have Task 7 say the four constructions gain an explicit `complexity` argument, that no default is added, and that `test_render.py` is in scope.

findings.title: Tasks 10 and 14 disagree on what a tokenizer `MemoryError` does
findings.description:
Task 10 (lines 121-123) says any of `token_errors` puts the file in `unparsed_files`, while a `MemoryError` during the pass gives `tool_failed`. Task 14 lists `MemoryError` as a TypeScript token error, mirroring `typescript_length.py:151`.

So a TypeScript tokenizer `MemoryError` lands in `unparsed_files`, while the same error in Python (Task 12) gives `tool_failed`. Task 11's test at line 139 pins only the `tool_failed` reading, and the slice's failure-mode table assigns `MemoryError` to `tool_failed`.

Fix: drop `MemoryError` from Task 14's token errors, or state the precedence in Task 10 and test it in Task 15.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes, not plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description:
All 17 commit points are written as `- [ ] Commit: ...` (lines 46, 68, 88, 97, 115, 142, 156, 171, 183, 191, 208, 229, 246, 262, 271, 276, 283), and line 290 is an 18th commit checkbox. A checkbox for the commit can only be ticked after the commit exists, which forces a follow-up commit that only checks boxes.

Fix: convert each to a plain `**Commit**: \`…\`` line. Placement itself is good: each sits after its test task at a green point, neither per-task nor end-only.

findings.title: Success Criterion 10's "other metrics are unchanged" has no test
findings.description:
Task 11 triggers the ceiling on `measure_duplication` in isolation, where no other metrics exist. No task asserts that file length, function length and complexity stay present when duplication is `tool_failed`. Success Criterion 10 and row 2 of the failure-mode table both require that outcome.

Fix: add one case to Task 13 through `PythonAdapter` with the ceiling lowered. No new task is needed.

findings.title: `tool_support.tool_failed` requires a `command` argument the tasks do not specify
findings.description: Tasks 10 and 23 route non-subprocess failures through `tool_failed`, whose `command` keyword is required and logged as "(command: …; stderr: …)". One line saying what to pass for the duplication pass and the Cobertura reader would remove a guess.

findings.title: Success criteria trace to tasks
findings.description:
Apart from the Success Criterion 10 clause above, every criterion has a task:

| Criterion | Tasks |
|---|---|
| 1, 2 | 8, 9 |
| 3 | 4, 6 |
| 4 | 11, 13, 15 |
| 5 | 22, 26 |
| 6, 7 | 18, 20, 24 |
| 8 | 20, 24 |
| 9 | 16, 17 |
| 10 | 11 |
| 11 | 26 |
| 12 | 7, 8 |
| Contract freeze | 25, 30 |
| Docs and CHANGELOG | 28 |
| Walkthrough | 29 |

All six failure-mode rows have a test asserting the signal. There is no scope creep, no merge or push task, and the slice restates no NFR, so no load test is owed.

findings.title: Sequencing and code references
findings.description:
- **Order:** dependencies are respected, and each implementation task is followed directly by its test task. Fixtures (18) precede the reader (19).
- **Metrics declaration:** each metric is added to `adapter.metrics` in the same task that returns it, which `take.py:69` requires.
- **References:** every helper I checked exists as described: `python_adapter.py:105`, `lengths._measure_source`, `_is_counted`, `repo_relative`, `FIXTURE_ROOT_TOKEN` and `read_fixture`, `run_git`, and the `.squadron.toml` exemption at `preflight.py:32`.
- **Gitignore:** `coverage.xml` and `.squadron.toml` are both gitignored, so walkthrough steps 3-7 will not dirty the tree.

findings.title: Proportionality
findings.description: Thirty tasks in one file fit a slice with five new modules, two languages, twelve functional criteria and a six-row failure table. The step detail is taken from D1-D6, not invented, and no test task goes beyond a stated criterion or failure mode.
